Hi Bill,

I am Hal, the technical side of the HeliumDeploy team. Sarah passed your pool question to me, and the answer is yes.

The Magic Miner 40T can mine to a normal pool.
Point it at your own node and mine solo for the full block reward, or at any pool
. Kryptex is a standard stratum pool, so it is just the usual three fields in the Harlo OS web interface: the stratum URL and port from Kryptex, your worker name, and the password (Kryptex accepts anything there, "x" is fine). You find the miner's IP on the front display, type it into a browser on the same network, and the pool settings are on that page. Nothing special, no custom build, no flashing.

The reason the listing leads with solo is marketing emphasis, not a limitation. The 40T is sold as a lottery machine because 40 TH/s against the whole network is a long shot at a full block, and that is the honest framing. On a pool you instead get small, steady payouts proportional to the shares you submit, which at 40 TH/s is a real but modest trickle. Both are supported by the same firmware. You can switch between them whenever you like, and you are not locked into either by the purchase.

One extra that is genuinely useful with your solar setup:
Harlo OS can also split the hashrate across up to four pools at once
.
JD split a unit three ways on camera, 10 TH/s to Bitcoin, 10 to Bitcoin Cash and 10 to a third pool
. So you could run, say, most of it solo for the lottery ticket and a slice to Kryptex so something lands in your wallet regularly.

On the fans, since that was one of your open points:
two 120 mm fans sit behind the front grille
, and they are the low hum type rather than a whine. Whether they are owner replaceable is the one piece we are still confirming with the maker rather than guessing at, and you will get that in writing here.

The B. 7 ship date and the written warranty terms are not mine to state, and I have put both back in front of the team this morning. A colleague is picking those up today.

If you want to talk pools or settings with people running these units daily, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there. He is the one who tested the unit on camera.

Hal, HeliumDeploy

I’ll also look forward to the written warranty terms, the Batch 7 ship date, and the answer on fan replacement once your team has them.
Thanks again, I appreciate the help.
Bill

Hi Bill,

The A. comparison is the right instinct. Harlo OS gives you preset modes and, past them, frequency and core voltage as numbers you type, with the stock values one click away if you push too far. The dashboard shows live hashrate, calibrated power at the wall and both temperatures, so you can watch what a change actually costs you in watts rather than guessing.

On the power range. The presets are Eco at 30 TH/s and 450 W rated, Standard at 40 TH/s and 650 W, and Turbo at 50 TH/s and 850 W. JD's wall meter on a test unit read 430 to 480 W in Eco, 620 W at 36.8 TH/s and 690 W at 41.4 TH/s in Standard, and past 815 W in Turbo with the fans at 100 percent. Worth repeating since you are buying for the long haul: Turbo is above the rated 40 TH/s, so it counts as overclocking and is not covered by the warranty. Below Eco you can hand tune the frequency and voltage lower, which is exactly what you would want on a thin solar day, but I do not have a measured floor figure for the 40T and I am not going to invent one. I have asked JD for a realistic lowest stable wall number, and whether frequency and voltage changes apply live from the web page or need a restart. On most of our BM1370 units the clock and voltage changes take effect through the ASIC PLL without a reboot, while a pool change does restart the mining session, but I want JD to confirm that on this specific unit before you hold me to it.

On a Bitcoin pool. Kryptex does run a Bitcoin pool as well as Ethereum Classic, so you can keep the same account if you like it. Among owners of these small units the common choices are public-pool.io and solo.ckpool.org if you want solo style lottery shots with your own payout address, and Ocean or Braiins if you want steady proportional payouts. All of them are plain stratum, so it is the same three fields either way. Given your solar surplus, a sensible setup is most of the hashrate on a solo pool for the block ticket and a slice on a payout pool so you see something arriving regularly, which the four pool split in Harlo OS lets you do in one unit.

On the delivered total. I cannot see pricing, shipping rates or tax, so I have put that in front of the team with your Florida address in mind. They are offline for tonight and pick it up at 10am Eastern tomorrow, and the quoted total will come to you in this thread along with the Batch 7 ship date, the written warranty terms and the fan replacement answer.

If you want to go deeper on the tuning side before then, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there. He answers most days, and there are owners running these on solar who will tell you what settings they settled on.

Hal, HeliumDeploy
